name: Sonata Software Ltd
title: Sonata Software Ltd - 532221 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

summary.headline: Sonata Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue fell 17.7% QoQ to Rs 2,536.2 Cr, while PAT rose 25% QoQ to Rs 130.5 Cr on International margin gains.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue of Rs 2,536.2 Cr declined 17.7% QoQ and 3.1% YoY, while PAT rose 25% QoQ to Rs 130.5 Cr. International services delivered EBITDA (before other income and forex) of 20.2%, up 70 bps QoQ, helped by utilisation of 91.8% and an offshore mix of 68%. Domestic business revenue of Rs 1,759.2 Cr was down 25% QoQ, and gross contribution fell 3.9% YoY as an OEM began direct billing some large customers. The call also covered a leadership transition: Rajsekhar Datta Roy was appointed CEO for International after Samir Dhir declined to extend his contract.

financial_highlights.change: flat QoQ; +0.6% QoQ in constant currency

financial_highlights.metric: International EBITDA before OI and forex Q4 FY26

segments.name: International services
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue of Rs 779.2 Cr (+5.5% QoQ in INR); EBITDA after OI and forex Rs 183.8 Cr (+25.2% QoQ). FY26 EBITDA after OI and forex Rs 607.7 Cr (+18% YoY); FY26 PAT Rs 292.7 Cr (+18.7% YoY).

segments.name: Domestic business
segments.commentary: Q4 gross contribution Rs 75.3 Cr (-1% QoQ, -3.9% YoY); Q4 PAT Rs 46.3 Cr (+3.9% QoQ). FY26 gross contribution Rs 288.7 Cr (-3.5% YoY). SMC and corporate segment grew about 27% YoY.

guidance_outlook: Management aims to maintain EBITDA at a similar level in the near term, with margins expected to stay similar in the short run.
Management is open to investing for AI-led growth, which could reduce margins if needed.
Domestic management expects a return to growth in FY27, with growth back to historical rates within one to two quarters.
International growth expected to continue at a similar trajectory in the short term; medium-term growth expected to be gradual.
Capex for FY27 expected at similar levels to FY26 on an annual basis; Q4 capex spike was a one-time Chennai facility for a large BFSI client.
No M&A plans at present; will wait a couple of quarters and may revisit in the medium term.
risks_watch: Domestic business: OEM direct billing risk, low-margin entry on new large deals, and dependence on delivering the growth return in FY27.
International: elongated client decision cycles driven by macro conditions; BFSI contraction risk at existing clients; sustainability of the TMT top-client upturn.
Margin trajectory: management may reinvest efficiency gains into growth, and utilisation may fall from the current 91.8% high.
Sharp consolidated revenue drop of 17.7% QoQ in Q4; watch whether the domestic revenue decline reverses.
Leadership transition: new International CEO in place about 15 days before the call; Samir Dhir's exit and the Board's succession planning are open items.
Large-deal pipeline count: management's explanation for the drop from 28-32 to 11 needs confirmation in next quarter's investor deck.
summary.management_tone: Cautiously optimistic: management highlighted the PAT and margin gains and AI-led order traction, but was guarded on demand, citing elongated decision cycles, macro headwinds and a new CEO still settling in. Specific FY27 growth and sub-vertical plans were deferred to a later update.
key_quotes: We remain cautiously optimistic and expect gradual improvement and growth over the medium term.
Our endeavor will be to maintain EBITDA at a similar level.
The reason pipeline would have come down is because we have announced two large deals this quarter.
we believe that during this fiscal year we should be back to our growth trajectory.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the strategy shift for International, investment focus by vertical and sub-vertical, medium-term growth, and the role of M&A.
qa_highlights.answer: Raj Datta Roy (about 15 days into the role) said verticals will continue, with sharper sub-vertical focus, investment in go-to-market, partnerships and AI delivery; specifics to follow in a couple of months. Jagannathan CN said there are no current M&A plans, to wait a couple of quarters and possibly revisit in the medium term.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked whether International margins can hold at 91.8% utilisation or whether investment will reduce them, and what the medium-term margin is.
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to a similar margin in the short run; utilisation may fall a little with business requirements; offshore mix (68%) is among the best. The company will invest if growth requires it. Endeavour is to maintain EBITDA at a similar level.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked why the large-deal pipeline count fell to 11 from the usual 28-32 range.
qa_highlights.answer: Shilpa Kolhatkar said the overall trajectory is unchanged and the drop reflects two large deals announced in the quarter. Jagannathan CN said the count is a point-in-time figure as of March 31 and that deals converted at year-end are no longer counted.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked when the Domestic business returns to growth on gross contribution and beta basis, and whether direct billing risk remains.
qa_highlights.answer: Sujit Mohanty said the earlier large-customer loss has been almost fully covered over four quarters and the business should return to its growth trajectory this fiscal year. Management does not expect further large-customer losses to direct billing, though it has no written policy from the OEM; two to three customers in discussion were moved to the partner route.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked what is holding back International traction despite AI focus, given the modest size of the business.
qa_highlights.answer: Raj Datta Roy said clients are taking larger AI bets rather than experiments, with green shoots especially in engineering, but decisions are elongated by the client's macro environment rather than technology capability.

qa_highlights.question: Analyst asked about the capex jump and the steady-state level, and whether the first-half capex annualised is a fair run-rate.
qa_highlights.answer: Jagannathan CN said the Q4 increase was a one-time Chennai facility for a large BFSI client. FY27 capex is expected at similar levels to FY26 on a full-year basis; first-half annualisation is not appropriate, and the full figure will be shared separately.

capex_capacity: Q4 FY26 capex spike was a one-time new facility in Chennai to serve one large BFSI customer; management said no plans to expand any other facility at present.
Management said FY27 capex is expected at similar levels to FY26 on an annual basis; the first-half annualised capex figure was not endorsed, with the full-year number to be shared separately.
Facilities were optimised where possible; the company had no comparable facility spend in earlier quarters.
Utilisation at 91.8% in Q4 FY26 (vs 90% in Q3); management said utilisation may come down a little depending on business requirements, having reached its best achievable level.
demand_pricing: International AI-led order book was $16.9 mn in Q4 FY26 and $49 mn for FY26, about 18% of total order book; AI-led pipeline $280 mn as of Q4 FY26.

Q4 FY26 order book $95 mn with book-to-bill of 1.16x; eight large deals won in FY26, two of them in Q4 (including a global fintech core banking modernisation and a multi-year managed services contract with a PE-backed B2B SaaS company).
Top 10 clients contributed 54% of revenue; 12 clients above $5 mn run-rate and 9 clients in the $3-5 mn band (up one from Q3); seven new customers added in Q4 and 23 in FY26.

Healthcare, HLS and BFSI together contributed 30% of Q4 FY26 revenue. BFSI remains under pressure from a large client ramp-down and possible contraction at existing clients; TMT top-client upturn described as early and under watch for sustainability.

Management said decision cycles are elongated due to the macro environment rather than technology; green shoots seen in engineering-led AI spend. Domestic business: OEM direct billing by one partner removed some large-customer revenue; management said no further large-customer losses expected and that growth should return within one to two quarters, with low-margin entry on new large deals built into plan.
Dynamics business has an AI-led pipeline; data business was hit by BFSI and RMD client ramp-downs. Management expects RMD to recover in FY27.

adds.what: One-time new facility in Chennai for one large BFSI customer (capex spike in Q4 FY26)

growth.why: Management guides to maintaining International EBITDA at a similar level and Domestic returning to growth within one to two quarters, backed by a $95 mn order book (1.16x book-to-bill) and an AI pipeline of $280 mn, but no quantified revenue growth target was given and medium-term growth is described as gradual.

mgmt.note: Rajsekhar Datta Roy appointed CEO for International after Samir Dhir declined to extend his contract; no stated growth plan beyond guidance of gradual medium-term growth.
